title: Kanchipuram silk sari
summary: Kanchipuram saris are woven in thick pure silk in the town of Kanchipuram in Tamil Nadu. The body and the broad border are often woven in contrasting colours and joined by interlocking the weft threads where they meet, and gold-coloured thread edges the shapes. Checks, stripes and flowers fill the body.
howToPlay: Pick a thread colour and a pattern shape from the tray.
Touch a square on the cloth to weave that shape there; it is mirrored on the other side of the centre line.
Copy the panel shown on the card, then press Check.
rules: The panel is mirrored left and right, so every shape you place also appears on its partner square.
A square counts only when its shape and its thread colour both match the pattern you are copying.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Kanchipuram silk is woven by families of weavers who have worked in the town for generations. Its weight comes from the thick silk and the gold-coloured thread, and a joined border in a strongly contrasting colour is one of its best-known features.
